question: is storm a triggered ability that can be countered?
miner_rationale: 702.40a spells out that storm is a triggered ability worded 'When you cast this spell, copy it...', which is exactly what the question asks and implies it goes on the stack and can be countered (while the copies it makes are not themselves cast).

question: can i use cards with hybrid mana symbols in a commander deck that only has one of those colors?
miner_rationale: You need the deck-construction restriction (903.5c) plus something establishing that a hybrid symbol contributes both colors, which either the color identity definition (903.4, 'any mana symbols in that card's mana cost or rules text') or the hybrid symbol rule (107.4e, 'a hybrid mana symbol is all of its component colors') supplies. Hence AND-of-ORs.

question: can I respond to the untap step?
miner_rationale: Both chunks independently state that no player receives priority during the untap step, so retrieving either one fully answers the question.

question: Do you cast lands?
miner_rationale: 305.1 and 116.2a each say the same thing from a different section: playing a land is a special action, it never uses the stack, and a land is never a spell. Either one answers 'no, you don't cast lands'.

question: can I sacrifice an evoked creature before that creature's evoke triggered ability resolves?
miner_rationale: 702.74a gives evoke's actual template ('When this permanent enters, if its evoke cost was paid, its controller sacrifices it'), which shows the sacrifice is a triggered ability that uses the stack and can therefore be responded to.

question: if a card loses all abilities, does that include keyword abilities?
miner_rationale: The question turns on keyword abilities being abilities at all; 702.1 and the Keyword Ability glossary entry each establish that a keyword is just shorthand for an ability, so losing all abilities removes them too.

question: can i draw cards if i'm already at my maximum hand size?
miner_rationale: 402.2 says a player may have any number of cards in hand and only discards down during the cleanup step, so drawing at seven is fine; the glossary entry restates the same limit.

question: what happens when a planeswalker has 0 or less loyalty counters?

question: what happens if i should draw a card when my library is empty?

question: what are the steps in combat and when do I have priority as the defending player?
miner_rationale: Two-part question: 506.1 is the only chunk listing the five combat steps in order, and the defending player's priority comes from the priority chain, which either 117.3a (active player gets it first each step) or 117.3d (it passes to the next player in turn order) explains.

question: can i respond to a mana ability?
miner_rationale: 605.3b states outright that a mana ability can't be targeted, countered, or otherwise responded to; 405.6c restates that mana abilities resolve immediately. Either answers 'no'.

question: can I respond to a cost being paid?
miner_rationale: Cost payment happens at 601.2h inside the uninterrupted casting process, and 601.2i is the point where the spell is actually cast and priority returns. You need both to see that there's no window to respond while costs are being paid.

question: how does the legend rule work?
miner_rationale: 704.5j is the legend rule state-based action verbatim, and the Legend Rule glossary entry restates it. Either hit answers the question.

question: when does my creature die after its been marked with a lethal amount of damage?
miner_rationale: The 'when' is the point of the question: 704.5g is the lethal-damage destruction condition, and 704.3 supplies the timing (checked whenever a player would get priority, not the instant damage is marked). Incomplete without both.

question: what happens during the cleanup step?
miner_rationale: The cleanup step is exactly three things: discard to maximum hand size (514.1), remove damage and end 'until end of turn' effects (514.2), and normally no player gets priority (514.3). Missing any one leaves the answer incomplete.

question: when are state-based actions checked?
miner_rationale: 704.3 and 117.5 describe the same check from the two sides (state-based actions and priority), each saying SBAs are performed whenever a player would get priority, before triggers go on the stack.

question: when can I concede a game?
miner_rationale: Three restatements of the same rule: a player may concede at any time and leaves the game immediately. Any single hit is a correct retrieval.

question: when someone other than the active player casts a spell, who gets priority first?
miner_rationale: 117.3c says the player who had priority when they cast a spell receives priority afterward, so the nonactive caster keeps it rather than handing it to the active player; 601.2i restates this at the end of the casting process.

question: when the active player cast a spell, who gets priority first?
miner_rationale: Same rule as the mirror question: under 117.3c (restated by 601.2i) the caster retains priority, so here the active player who cast the spell gets it back first.

question: can I hold priority to cast more spells after I've cast one or more spells?
miner_rationale: Holding priority is just 117.3c: casting a spell hands priority straight back to you, so you can keep casting before anyone responds. 601.2i states the same thing inside the casting rules.
